'''Chen Lan-bo''' ({{lang-zh|t=陳良博}}; born August 23, 1943) is a Taiwanese [[cellular biologist]], [[pathologist]], and [[biotechnologist]]. He was a professor of pathology at [[Harvard Medical School]] between 1977 and 2004 and is the author of over 250 publications. He is also a member of Boston's [[Dana–Farber Cancer Institute|Dana-Farber Cancer Institute]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=$45M in private financing vaults Synta's profile - Boston Business Journal |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/boston/stories/2002/11/11/story5.html|website=www.bizjournals.com|date=11 November 2002 |access-date=2020-01-20}}</ref> in the department of cancer and biology and a member of [[Academia Sinica]] in Taiwan.

==Early life and education==
Chen was born on 23 August 1943 in [[Yilan County, Taiwan|Yilan County]] during the [[Japanese rule of Taiwan]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.delos.capital/dr-lan-bo-chen/|title=Dr. Lan Bo Chen {{!}} Delos Capital|language=en-US|access-date=2020-01-20}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Lan-Bo Chen, CHO Pharma Inc: Profile and Biography - Bloomberg Markets|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/profile/person/20983640|access-date=2020-01-20|website=Bloomberg.com}}</ref> He graduated from [[National Taiwan University]] with a [[Bachelor of Science]] (B.S.) in 1968, then completed graduate studies in the United States, earning a [[Master of Science]] (M.S.) in 1972 and his [[Ph.D.]] in cell biology in 1975, both from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) under biologist [[John Buchanan (biologist)|John Buchanan]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=院士簡歷 |url=https://academicians.sinica.edu.tw/index.php?r=academician-n/show&id=110&_lang=en |access-date=2025-02-17 |website=academicians.sinica.edu.tw}}</ref>

==Research and career==
Chen did postdoctoral research work for one year supervised by [[James Watson|James D. Watson]], the Nobel laureate who co-discovered the DNA [[Nucleic acid double helix|double helix]] structure.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.biospace.com/delos-capital-announces-the-launch-of-curamir-therapeutics-inc-with-a-10-million-series-a-to-develop-mirna-based-cancer-therapeutics|title=Delos Capital Announces the Launch of Curamir Therapeutics Inc. with a $10 Million Series A to Develop miRNA-based Cancer Therapeutics|website=BioSpace|language=en-US|access-date=2020-01-20}}</ref> He did research on the mitogenicity of [[thrombin]] and surface alterations on mouse [[splenocyte]]s and also on intercellular LETS [[glycoprotein]] matrices.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Chen|first1=L. B.|last2=Teng|first2=N. N. H.|last3=Buchanan|first3=J. M.|date=1976-08-01|title=Mitogenicity of thrombin and surface alterations on mouse splenocytes|journal=Experimental Cell Research|volume=101|issue=1|pages=41–46|doi=10.1016/0014-4827(76)90409-2|pmid=986310|issn=0014-4827}}</ref>

He is also a cell biologist making seminal findings in the multiple fields of molecular cell biology and cancer biology, including the discovery of [[rhodamine 123]] for highly specific fluorescent localization of [[Mitochondrion|mitochondria]] in living cells, removal of [[carcinoma]] cells from contaminated bone marrow using the [[Lipophilicity|lipophilic cation]], identification of human cancer line without any Intermediate filaments, and also on the development of the rare event detection system to detect lung cancer cells from Body fluids.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lampidis|first1=Theodore J.|last2=Salet|first2=Christian|last3=Moreno|first3=Giuliana|last4=Chen|first4=Lan Bo|date=1984-09-01|title=Effects of the mitochondrial probe rhodamine 123 and related analogs on the function and viability of pulsating myocardial cells in culture|journal=Agents and Actions|language=en|volume=14|issue=5|pages=751–757|doi=10.1007/BF01978920|pmid=6475672|s2cid=1341638|issn=1420-908X}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Johnson|first1=Lincoln V.|last2=Summerhayes|first2=Ian C.|last3=Chen|first3=Lan Bo|date=1982-01-01|title=Decreased uptake and retention of rhodamine 123 by mitochondria in feline sarcoma virus-transformed mink cells|journal=Cell|volume=28|issue=1|pages=7–14|doi=10.1016/0092-8674(82)90369-5|pmid=6279315|s2cid=38032526|issn=0092-8674}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lampidis|first1=T. J.|last2=Bernal|first2=S. D.|last3=Summerhayes|first3=I. C.|last4=Chen|first4=L. B.|date=February 1983|title=Selective toxicity of rhodamine 123 in carcinoma cells in vitro|journal=Cancer Research|volume=43|issue=2|pages=716–720|issn=0008-5472|pmid=6848187}}</ref>

In the early days of his career, he worked as a Senior Staff investigator at the Cold Spring Harbor Laboratories, before becoming a full and emeritus professor of pathology at the [[Harvard Medical School]] with laboratories at the [[Dana–Farber Cancer Institute|Dana-Farber Cancer Institute]].

Chen founded Synta Pharmaceuticals Corporation,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Willis |first1=Randall C. |title=Bad news for Beantown?|url=http://pubs.acs.org/subscribe/archive/mdd/v07/i09/html/904feature_willis2.html |access-date=1 January 2019 |work=ACS Publications |date=September 2004}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Connolly |first1=Allison |title=$45M in private financing vaults Synta's profile |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/boston/stories/2002/11/11/story5.html |access-date=2 January 2019 |work=Boston Business Journal |date=11 November 2002}}</ref> and in 2007, was invited to serve on the founding board of directors for Yu Chang Biologics Company, also known as TaiMed Biologics Company.<ref name="taimedstart">{{cite news |title=New AIDS research firm to be created |url=https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/biz/archives/2007/09/14/2003378726 |access-date=1 January 2019 |work=Taipei Times |date=14 September 2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Kao |first1=Cameron |title=Biomedical industry gets a clean bill of health: expert |url=https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/biz/archives/2014/07/08/2003594581 |access-date=1 January 2019 |work=Taipei Times |date=8 July 2014}}</ref> Chen was supportive of [[Tsai Ing-wen]]'s 2012 presidential campaign after Tsai's involvement with TaiMed became a subject of investigation.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Chang |first1=Rich |title=Tsai cleared of Yu Chang allegations |url=https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/front/archives/2012/08/15/2003540320 |access-date=1 January 2019 |work=Taipei Times |date=15 August 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Wang |first1=Chris |title=2012 ELECTIONS: Key figures speak out to support Tsai |url=https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/front/archives/2011/12/16/2003520854 |access-date=1 January 2019 |work=Taipei Times |date=16 December 2011}}</ref> Chen described the [[Sunflower Student Movement]] of 2014 as "the mightiest movement Taiwan has seen in several decades" and said that "this student movement will kick-start the development of Taiwan’s biotech industry."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Huang |first1=Tien-lien |title=Sunflower movement helped lift economy |url=https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/editorials/archives/2014/07/10/2003594743 |access-date=1 January 2019 |work=Taipei Times |date=10 July 2014}}</ref> In January 2019, Chen signed a petition opposing the confirmation of [[Kuan Chung-ming]] as president of National Taiwan University.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Maxon |first1=Ann |title=Academics ask ministry to annul Kuan appointment |url=https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2019/01/02/2003707209 |access-date=2 January 2019 |work=Taipei Times |date=2 January 2019}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Chen received the [[American Cancer Society]] Professor award,<ref name=nas>{{cite web|url=https://db1n.sinica.edu.tw/textdb/ioconas/binfo1N.php?_op=?ID:L052|title=sinica.edu|website=sinica.edu.tw}}</ref> and, in 1996, was elected as a member of the Academia Sinica.<ref>{{cite news |title=Lan-Bo Chen |url=https://academicians.sinica.edu.tw/index.php?r=academician-n%2Fshow&id=110 |access-date=8 September 2023 |publisher=Academia Sinica}}</ref> He also served as a former board member at Madrigal Pharmaceuticals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://people.equilar.com/bio/lan-chen-madrigal-pharmaceuticals-inc/949077|title=Dr. Lan Bo Chen Ph.D.- Executive Bio, Work History, and Contacts - Equilar BoardEdge|website=people.equilar.com|access-date=2020-01-20}}</ref>
